- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slope or shift downward by 1–3%.
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., >89.5) with sentiment mostly positive (≥0.67), it often overshoots; cap forecast at 92–94% of prior peak or adjust downward 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- If true outcome shows sharp drop after recent spike (e.g., 90+ → 80–85), model often fails to correct; apply mean reversion rule: subtract 2–5% from forecast if sentiment turns negative or neutral.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values (neutral/negative), model tends to underestimate; add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for underconfidence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overfits recent highs; apply lag correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast if last 3–5 days show no significant drop.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and model is flat or rising slowly, it may miss momentum; increase forecast slope by 0.5–1% per day if sentiment remains above 0.7.
